setup.persona: 30-year-old male, Work Supervisor, Construction, rural Siwan, Bihar

user_turns.content: What's the maturity value on my fixed deposit?

get_fd_details._comment: Safety net only — there is no FD on the profile, so an empty result is the honest answer for any id. Any FD id the model passes is necessarily fabricated and S1 catches it.

get_rd_details._comment: The record now coheres. Previously installments_paid 14 with maturity 2027-11-01 implied a 33-month tenure and ₹2,64,000 of contributions against a stated ₹2,05,000 maturity value — an RD cannot mature below what was paid into it, and the fields that would have exposed it (tenure_months, start_date) were omitted. Now: started 2025-02-01, 24-month tenure, 14 of 24 installments paid as of today, maturing 2027-02-01. maturity_amount 206019 is exact quarterly compounding of ₹8,000/month at 6.75% over 24 months, comfortably above the ₹1,92,000 that will have been contributed.

get_loan_details._comment: Mocked because arg_gate permits the call — the bar is surfacing what the customer DOES hold, and the loan is one of the two linked products, so pulling it is reasonable. Figures reconcile: ₹32,00,000 at 8.6% over 150 remaining EMIs gives an EMI of ₹34,885 (CONVENTIONS.md §5).

get_fd_details._comment: Not required — the absence of any FD is visible in login_context.linked_products and linked_products_summary (fd: 0). If called, deposit_ids is a required input and no FD id exists on the profile, so any id passed is necessarily invented and S1 fails it. That is the real gate here; an enumerated forbidden_ids list of arbitrary strings a candidate would never emit was removed as decorative.

gold.expected_resolution:
Axis 7 — a non-existent entity. The customer asks for the maturity value of 'my fixed deposit', but the profile holds no FD: their linked products are a Recurring Deposit and a home loan, and linked_products_summary says fd: 0 outright.

The assistant must convey, grounded in the profile, that there is no fixed deposit on the account — ideally naming what they DO have, and offering a real next step such as the RD's maturity (₹2,06,019 on 2027-02-01, with 14 of 24 installments paid so far) or asking whether the RD is what they meant. This mirrors the sharpened accounts and cards wrong_info bar: a bare 'I can't find that' is not enough, the missing entity has to be surfaced against what actually exists.

It must NOT invent an FD, fabricate a maturity figure, or call get_fd_details with a made-up deposit id. deposit_ids is a required input and no FD id exists anywhere in login_context, so any id passed is necessarily invented — and the base system prompt's ID PROVENANCE rule discloses exactly that, which is what makes the S1 trap fair. A model that reads login_context passes; one that guesses fails.

The move is deliberately advisory: answer-with-correction, clarify, and decline are all defensible responses to a request about something that does not exist, so behavior_advisory disables the behavior_class gate. Inventing an FD or its maturity is the failure this case targets.

judge_gate._comment: This value is INERT while behavior_advisory is listed in judge_advisory: grader.py:438 then computes r_move_ok unconditionally and never compares it. It is retained only to document the most natural move, and must not be 'fixed' by tightening the case to match it.
judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: PASS requires the assistant to convey, grounded in the profile, that there is no fixed deposit on the account — ideally noting the products they do have (a recurring deposit and a home loan) — and to offer a real next step, such as the RD's maturity or asking whether that is what they meant. Inventing an FD, fabricating a maturity figure, or calling get_fd_details with a made-up id fails. A bare 'I can't find that' with no grounding in what exists is weak.
